query: What are best practices for consent and assent with minors in low-literacy settings (scripts, documentation, age bands, verbal and witnessed consent)?

response.query: What are best practices for consent and assent with minors in low-literacy settings (scripts, documentation, age bands, verbal and witnessed consent)?
response.answer: Best practices for consent with minors in low-literacy settings include verbal, witnessed consent and assent from the minor, with documentation in simple language. Age-appropriate explanations are crucial, and guardians should be involved. Ensure consent is clear and understood.

results.title: Adoption and Children Act (Northern Ireland) 2022
results.content: ## Changes over time for: Adoption and Children Act (Northern Ireland) 2022. This version of this Act contains provisions that are prospective.Help about Status. The term provision is used to describe a definable element in a piece of legislation that has legislative effect – such as a Part, Chapter or section. Adoption and Children Act (Northern Ireland) 2022 is up to date with all changes known to be in force on or before 14 May 2026. #### Considerations applying to the exercise of powersN.I. 1.—(1) This section applies whenever a court or adoption agency is coming to a decision relating to the adoption of a child. (6) The court or adoption agency must always consider the whole range of powers available to it in the child’s case (whether under this Act or the Children Order); and the court must not make any order under this Act unless it considers that making the order would be better for the child than not doing so.

results.title: Negative Option Rule - Federal Register
results.content: In addition to these deception-based requirements, the Commission has repeatedly stated billing consumers without consumers' express informed consent is an unfair act under the FTC Act.[[17](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2024/11/15/2024-25534/negative-option-rule#footnote-17-p90478)]. Given the persistence of unfair and deceptive practices despite significant law enforcement attention at both the Federal and State level, the Commission published its 2019 advance notice of proposed rulemaking (“ANPR”) seeking comments on the current Rule, as well as possible new measures to reduce consumer harm created by deceptive or unfair negative option marketing.[[38](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2024/11/15/2024-25534/negative-option-rule#footnote-38-p90479)]  Specifically, the Commission sought comment on various alternatives, including amendments to existing rules to further address disclosures, consumer consent, and cancellation. On November 4, 2021, the Commission published an “Enforcement Policy Statement Regarding Negative Option Marketing” (“2021 Enforcement Policy Statement” or “EPS”) to provide guidance regarding its enforcement of  ( printed page 90480)  various statutes and FTC regulations.[[41](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2024/11/15/2024-25534/negative-option-rule#footnote-41-p90480)]  The 2021 Enforcement Policy Statement enunciated various principles rooted in FTC case law and restated previous guidance related to the provision of information to consumers, consent, and cancellations.
